identification_flow: A customer is identified by 5 identifiers: cart_id (soft), cookie (soft), email_id (hard), phone_id (hard), qa_new_id (soft). cart_id is set by a standalone identify call when the checkout page loads via Shopify storefront together with cookie, and also by a standalone identify call when the checkout page loads together with cookie. Events that send it in customer_ids: banner, campaign, cart_update, checkout, page_visit, purchase, purchase_item, session_end and 1 more. cookie is set by a standalone identify call on the first page view of a new visitor via Shopify storefront; view_category, view_item, wishlist_update are sent with cookie only and are merged into the profile through it. Other events that send it in customer_ids: banner, campaign, checkout, newsletter_signup, page_visit, search, session_end, session_start. email_id is set when the newsletter_signup event fires through the SDK identify call. Events that send it in customer_ids: banner, campaign, consent, newsletter_signup, page_visit, purchase, purchase_item, session_end and 1 more. phone_id is set by a standalone identify call when the SMS consent form is submitted together with cookie. Other events that send it in customer_ids: banner, campaign, page_visit, session_end, session_start. qa_new_id is set at a moment no trigger records yet. No event sends it in customer_ids yet. No identification act is defined yet for passenger_id (soft). Soft identifiers recognise an anonymous visitor; a hard identifier ties that visitor to a known customer, so an event that carries one identifies the customer by it.

use_cases.name: Abandoned cart
use_cases.narrative:
Abandoned cart is a marketing use case. Recovers carts abandoned after an add-to-cart event with no completed checkout.

## Flow

1. The site sends `cart_update[action=add]` with required `product_id`, `total_price`.
2. The site sends `checkout`.

## Customer data

- Customer property `email` (required).

use_cases.name: Purchase confirmation
use_cases.narrative:
Purchase confirmation is a transactional use case. Sends a confirmation email for every successful purchase, with its line items.

## Flow

1. The site sends `purchase[purchase_status=completed]` with required `purchase_id`, `total_price`.
2. The site sends `purchase_item` with required `price`, `quantity`.

## Customer data

- Customer property `email` (required).

use_cases.name: Back in stock
use_cases.narrative:
Back in stock is a marketing use case. Notifies a customer when a viewed, out-of-stock product becomes available again.

## Flow

1. The site sends `view_item` with required `product_id`, `stock_level`.

## Customer data

- Customer property `phone` (optional).

## Gaps

- (removed): No event named "wishlist_add" in this project. wishlist_add is not tracked yet; the wishlist_update event covers adds, map or rename it.

unattached_findings.message: Property "price" is observed with inconsistent JSON types across events: number, string.
product catalogs differ: field "stock_level" has different types (products_cz (CZ / cs-CZ): string, products_gb (GB / en-GB): number).
Consent category "personalization" has no standard_key tag, while at least one standard consent key has no mapping.
Consent category "whatsapp_updates" has no standard_key tag, while at least one standard consent key has no mapping.
A Catalog exists in the definition, but the mapping's catalogs.main and catalogs.variant are both empty.
